A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures and appendices. The original proofs and experiments can be matched across versions; v1 Appendices D and E become v2 Appendices E and F.

before.justification: Figures 2–6 report original Gaussian simulations and Color-MNIST/CIFAR-10 experiments using linear regression, random features and neural networks.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Figures 7–8 add multiclass Color-MNIST, correlation-strength sweeps and corrupted CIFAR-10 results.

M1.justification: The ridge-regression and random-feature procedures remain unchanged. Appendix F.1 adds a limited multiclass adaptation of the two-layer network, using one-hot targets and class-logit outputs trained with MSE, extending v1's binary prediction setup.

E1.justification: Appendix F.1 substantially broadens evaluation coverage from binary Color-MNIST to all ten digits and adds corrupted CIFAR-10 boats/trucks with label-correlated brightness and glass-blur corruptions. These introduce multiclass task requirements and different spurious input conditions; existing coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated model families remain linear regression, random features and two-layer ReLU networks. Comparator membership in the original experiments is unchanged, and the added experiments reuse these families without introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: The original protocols are retained. New experiments introduce multiclass evaluation using the parity of the highest-logit class to compute C, additional correlation settings, and corrupted CIFAR-10 with alpha = 0.95 and a width-1000 neural network. These are settings for added experiments, not revisions to the original runs.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds sensitivity analysis of binary Color-MNIST across several color–digit correlations, testing their effects on loss and C throughout the regularization sweep. V1's corresponding experiment used a fixed correlation. Existing covariance, whitening and out-of-distribution analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix E and v2 Appendix F both specify averages over 10 independent trials with one-standard-deviation shading and the same sources of randomness. No changed run-count or uncertainty-estimation practice is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 7–8 add substantial result sets for multiclass prediction, correlation sensitivity and corrupted inputs. The binary sweep shows greater C with stronger color–digit correlation; the corruption experiments report nonzero C at small regularization and declining C at large regularization. Original Figures 2–6 retain their plotted results; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V2 adds the gradient-flow solution in Equation (5.6) and an additive-feature formulation, including covariance expressions, in Appendix D. The main theorems, assumptions and substantive proofs remain intact. Appendix D sketches an extension rather than proving corresponding full guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about characterizing spurious correlations, regularization and simplicity bias, the loss trade-off, and random-feature/linear-regression equivalence.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly connects easier spurious features with faster learning through gradient-flow eigendirections. Appendix D discusses applicability beyond concatenated features and qualifies the interpretation of C: it need not vanish at theta-hat = theta-star when features combine additively.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit public-code repository pointer and describes the new multiclass encoding, correlation construction and corruption choices. Existing data-generation instructions and original neural-network training settings are retained. Repository contents or functionality are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. on logit correction and Loureiro et al. on teacher–student learning curves. It also distinguishes its converged-solution analysis from previously cited training-dynamics work. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammatical, notation and explanatory edits, clarifies asymptotic regimes and source notation, and inserts Appendix D and subsection F.1. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the multipanel Figures 7 and 8 and resizes/repositions Figures 4 and 5 side by side. Existing figure graphics are retained, with limited caption and surrounding-layout adjustments rather than a document-wide redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support beyond v1's binary image tasks through multiclass, correlation-sensitivity and corrupted-input experiments. The code-access pointer and explicit discussion of overlapping features improve reproducibility documentation and interpretation. These are incremental gains: the central theory and original evidence remain unchanged, and the additive-feature extension is only partially developed.
